metadata.title: The Well-Tempered clAIvier
metadata.subtitle: Prelude IV in C-sharp minor — new composition study
metadata.character: One rhythmic gesture exchanged and intensified
composition_notes: Completely new, literally authored 32-bar prelude. No notes from the earlier Prelude IV are reused as a compositional template.
The opening sixteenth-unit rhythm 2,1,1,2,3,1,1,1 drives toward a target held across beat 3, followed by a descending tail.
The bass receives the gesture in bars 5-6 and 17-18; the upper line continues across changing bass harmony with prepared suspensions.
E major is approached by actual 4-3 suspensions; E7 turns to A, then the C# dominant to F# minor.
Bar 20 expands the rising portion of the cell, recovering the original register before the tonic return.
The returning idea leads to a higher C# in bar 25, faster bass harmonic movement, ii half-diminished and a dominant pedal; only the final bar gives the closing tonic.
This study is newly composed for listening and musical judgment, not certified as Bach-level writing or strict-species counterpoint.

composition_record.method: Literal authorship of both full lines; no chord-template generation, constraint search or automatic pitch repair.
composition_record.basis: New audition study responding to the listener critique of rhythmic inertia and decorative stylistic blocks.
